Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates software engineering by asking a model to generate a patch that fixes a real GitHub issue in a Python repository, validated by running the project’s tests. The “Verified” subset consists of tasks that have been human-verified as solvable with the provided repository state and test harness, reducing label noise and unsound tasks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends the SWE-bench patch-generation setup beyond Python to multiple programming languages, testing whether models can apply debugging and code-editing skills across language ecosystems. Tasks still require producing repository patches that satisfy tests, but with additional variability in toolchains, conventions, and library APIs.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a harder, more contamination-resistant software engineering benchmark designed to better reflect industrial coding tasks across multiple languages and larger, more complex repos. Models must produce correct patches under stricter evaluation conditions, with tasks intended to be more diverse and less prone to memorization than earlier coding benchmarks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic coding and systems work by giving tasks that must be completed inside a command-line environment using shell commands, files, and programming tools. Success depends on producing correct artifacts (code, configs, outputs) under realistic constraints such as dependency management, debugging, and iterative verification.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp evaluates research-oriented browsing agents on information-seeking questions that require multi-step web navigation and synthesis rather than single-page lookup. Models must plan search strategies, collect evidence across documents, and produce grounded answers under constraints meant to reduce irreproducibility from changing web content.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension

Description: τ2-bench measures interactive, policy-constrained tool use in simulated real-world customer-support settings (e.g., retail, airline, telecom), where an agent must converse with a user and call APIs to resolve tasks. It stresses maintaining consistent adherence to domain policies over multi-turn dialogues while completing user goals.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension, Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making (minor)
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control

Description: OSWorld evaluates multimodal computer-use agents that operate a desktop-like environment to complete tasks by interacting with GUIs, applications, and system settings. Agents must perceive screen state, choose actions (click/typing/navigation), and execute long-horizon workflows robustly across diverse tasks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Planning, Decision-making, Sensorimotor Coordination (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid-reasoning benchmark where models infer abstract transformation rules from a few input–output grid examples and apply them to new grids. It is designed to emphasize novel pattern induction and generalization over memorized knowledge, with limited examples per task.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon autonomous agency in a simulated business environment where an agent manages a vending-machine operation over many steps (e.g., inventory, pricing, supplier negotiation). Performance is scored by end-of-horizon business outcomes, encouraging sustained coherence, strategy, and adaptation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas evaluates real-world tool use via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), testing whether a model can discover appropriate tools, invoke them correctly, and chain multiple calls into a workflow. Tasks emphasize robustness to API details, error handling, and synthesizing outputs into a correct final response.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates agent performance on tasks representative of an entry-level financial analyst, such as interpreting financial documents, building or checking analyses, and producing justified recommendations. Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity capabilities by having models find known vulnerabilities and sometimes uncover new ones in real open-source projects given task descriptions and codebases. It measures practical security reasoning: understanding code behavior, identifying exploit-relevant patterns, and producing correct vulnerability findings or patches.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench evaluates the ability to understand, edit, and compute over complex spreadsheets derived from real-world scenarios. L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GPQA Diamond is a high-quality subset of GPQA consisting of difficult multiple-choice graduate-level science questions designed to be resistant to simple web search (“Google-proof”). L1:

L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)
